deepseek_columns.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sensor get 'TEMP_MB_PSU1_IN, TEMP_MB_PSU2_IN' 2>&1; echo ---SDR-FALLBACK---; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sdr elist 2>&1 | head -100
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: returns FULL raw `ipmitool (OOB lanplus) sensor get "<SENSOR>"` reading + threshold; user judges (read-only).

historical_reviews.deepseek: YES sends both names as one quoted comma-containing operand, which may match neither record. It does not distinguish motherboard sensors near PSU inlets from PSU-internal PMBus temperatures or prove slot identity, module population, thresholds, freshness or UI mapping.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly requires separate PSU1/PSU2 reads and inventory mapping. V3.1 further treats the `MB` prefix as a required sensor-source distinction, binds each result to the physical bay and installed PSU serial, and keeps PMBus telemetry only as mapped corroboration.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 876/2291 accepts one combined operand and output presence without separate record status, board-versus-PSU source identity, bay/serial mapping, redundancy state or complete UI/spec evidence.

original_test_intent: Verify the two motherboard PSU-inlet temperature records, `TEMP_MB_PSU1_IN` and `TEMP_MB_PSU2_IN`, are individually readable in Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading and correctly mapped to their physical PSU bays with specification-compliant values, units, status and supported thresholds.
original_method: Resolve the two records separately, establish whether each originates from a motherboard probe at the PSU inlet rather than the PSU's internal PMBus sensor, bind it to the physical bay and installed-module inventory, and compare complete passive raw/UI fields with the approved specification under recorded load and airflow. Preserve logs and PSU state.
manual_activity: The platform owner identifies the physical PSU bays, installed modules and whether each `MB_PSU*_IN` value is a board probe or PSU-provided channel, then defines per-bay acceptance. Automation can collect both records and UI rows separately; a human resolves source/bay ambiguity and owns the verdict. No PSU removal, feed change or load stimulus is authorized.
required_inputs: Exact chassis/board/BMC/BIOS configuration, PSU bay numbering, AC-feed topology, installed PSU serial/PN/FRU and redundancy state
For each label, the physical sensing point and source path, including any PMBus/I2C controller/address/channel only if applicable
Stable SDR name/number/type/entity/instance and Dashboard/Server Health row for PSU1_IN and PSU2_IN
Per-sensor units, scaling/rounding, tolerance, threshold capability/values/hysteresis, health, freshness and absent-module semantics
Recorded system power/load, fan policy/speeds, inlet/airflow condition, time alignment and approved reference-delta rules
Validated ipmitool/API/browser versions, protected authentication and pinned reviewed `sensor.git` revision/checksum or manual method
safety_requirements: Do not clear SEL or system logs; existing power, PSU, PMBus and thermal events establish the configuration and health context.
Do not pass `'TEMP_MB_PSU1_IN, TEMP_MB_PSU2_IN'` as one sensor identifier unless explicitly documented. Query the two stable records independently and keep their return/status evidence separate.

Do not assume the labels are PSU-internal PMBus temperature channels. Prove the motherboard-probe or module-source path and physical bay association; corroborating PMBus data must be separately identified.

Do not remove/reseat a PSU, disable an AC feed, change redundancy or power cap, add workload, obstruct airflow or alter thresholds. Those actions affect service/power safety and are outside this passive row.
Apply population-aware acceptance: an absent PSU may alter sensor availability only as the approved platform specification says. Never infer physical presence solely from a stale named record.

Do not truncate inventory, expose passwords using `-P`, assume cipher 17 or execute the unavailable Script before review. Stop without automatic retry on duplicated/swapped bay identity, stale data or UI/OOB/FRU disagreement.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target, PSU inventory/feed/bay map, sensor source, client and Script; establish a two-row expected matrix before collection.
Retrieve PSU1_IN and PSU2_IN independently with complete SDR identity, value, units, supported thresholds, status and timestamp; capture each unchanged Dashboard and Server Health row.
Correlate each record with physical bay and installed FRU and, if approved, time-aligned PMBus/reference telemetry under recorded redundancy/load/airflow state.
Preserve raw/redacted evidence and logs; perform no PSU/feed/power/load/fan/threshold mutation, automatic retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve bay numbering and installed PSU/AC-feed inventory and identify the true source/placement of both `MB_PSU*_IN` sensors.
Provide per-bay threshold, tolerance, status, freshness and absent-module rules plus any valid PMBus/reference correlation, and approve the tool/Script.
Review PSU1 and PSU2 evidence independently and issue the formal verdict without allowing one bay or a PSU-internal temperature to substitute for a motherboard inlet probe.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Unfit as written unless the platform literally defines the comma-containing label, because `sensor get` normally expects a single record identifier. It also does not prove board-versus-module source or bay/FRU mapping, truncates fallback output, exposes credentials and assumes cipher support.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Enumerate the complete repository, resolve exact PSU1_IN and PSU2_IN records and source paths, query each via protected read-only access and correlate both UI rows with the physical bay plus installed PSU inventory.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Both source names, Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading, readability/specification Criteria, generic clear text, Script URL, DeepSeek command and 1/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review corrects the combined-operand interpretation without editing Master or servicing PSUs.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a two-row evidence matrix keyed by physical PSU bay and stable motherboard-sensor identity, attach installed FRU/feed/source information, then compare complete raw/API and both UI values with per-bay specifications at a recorded passive power/airflow state.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The exact chassis, board, PSU population/feed configuration and BMC/SDR/WebUI build documented by the Project.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record board, BIOS/BMC/SDR/WebUI, PSU PN/serial/firmware, redundancy mode, management client and Script revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Board sensor-placement/PSU-bay drawings, PSU inventory and PMBus map where applicable, SDR thermal limits, WebUI schema and Project configuration specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Separates the two command operands, proves source and bay identity and adds population/redundancy/operating context while keeping the original passive display check.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Static motherboard inlet values do not validate PSU-internal telemetry, hot-swap, redundancy failover, AC-feed loss, load response, alarm assertion or protection behavior.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Bay/FRU/feed and source map, per-sensor acceptance, load/airflow/timing rules, protected tool or reviewed Script and evidence contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Bay numbering may differ among chassis, FRU and BMC; a removed module can leave a board probe active; PMBus and motherboard locations may legitimately report different temperatures.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use Redfish/OEM or PMBus telemetry as an approved alternate/corroboration only while preserving the original ipmitool method, recording interface/version/source and reason, obtaining engineer approval and proving separate bay-bound identity, value, threshold, status and freshness equivalence. PSU-internal temperature is not automatically equivalent to the named motherboard inlet sensor.
expected_evidence: Chassis/board/BMC/BIOS identity, physical bay numbering, AC-feed/redundancy state and installed PSU PN/serial/FRU inventory
Separate PSU1_IN and PSU2_IN complete raw records with stable IDs, source/placement, values, units, threshold capabilities/values, status and timestamps
Separate redacted Dashboard and Server Health evidence mapped to the same physical bays and sensor sources
Per-bay Project specification and recorded system load, fan speeds and airflow with approved tolerance/update-lag and optional PMBus/reference comparison
Explicit absent, missing, duplicate, swapped, stale or UI/OOB/FRU disagreement disposition and pinned Script/tool security evidence
No-clear/no-write/no-PSU-service/no-stress/no-retry proof, final power redundancy/BMC health, limitations and engineer-owned per-bay verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Items clearly list two motherboard PSU-inlet sensors and the Procedure/Criteria consistently require passive UI/spec comparison. DeepSeek's combined syntax is flawed, but exact source/bay mapping and acceptance are Project readiness inputs rather than an irreducible source contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The two-target passive purpose is clear. The Project can provide bay/source mapping, population rules and expected values, so the case is PACKAGE rather than permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on hybrid classification while sharpening the motherboard-versus-PMBus source distinction and installed FRU/feed evidence requirements.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces command-presence reasoning with separate query status, physical bay/source identity and population-aware acceptance.

review_improvement: Prevents a failed combined query, swapped PSU-bay labels or PSU-internal telemetry from being presented as two motherboard inlet sensors, and avoids unsafe PSU service to create evidence for a static case.
independent_technical_reasoning: The `MB` prefix suggests board-level sensing near PSU bays, so a PSU PMBus temperature cannot be assumed equivalent. The two comma-separated names require separate query results. Meaningful acceptance also needs physical bay and installed FRU mapping because BMC numbering can differ from chassis labels and an empty bay may still have an active motherboard probe.
